title: Nonzero-mode cancellation and the heat coefficient
notes: \(m[S;T]=m[S]=4^s m[0]\), \(B_4=n+m\); nonzero modes cancel in supergravity, leaving zero modes.

title: The exceptional Jordan algebra and compact F4
notes: Take Hermitian \(3\times3\) octonionic matrices with product \((AB+BA)/2\); their automorphism group is \(F_4\).

title: Formal Birkhoff normal form at a nonresonant elliptic equilibrium
notes: Arnold: \(H=\sum\omega_k z_k\bar z_k+\cdots\) reduces to \(H(\Pi_k)\), \(\Pi_k=z_k\bar z_k\), if the frequencies are independent; explicitly at the level of formal series.

title: Electron--positron annihilation and its inverse
notes: Dirac theory predicts positrons; an electron and positron can annihilate into two photons, and two photons can produce an electron--positron pair.

title: Hamilton's square-root relations and the missing quaternion quotient
notes: Three symbols square to \(-1\) and anticommute; adding the identity is said to give the quaternions.
statement: The universal unital real algebra with \(a^2=b^2=c^2=-1\) and pairwise anticommutation is \(\operatorname{Cl}_{0,3}\), of dimension eight, isomorphic to \(\mathbb H\oplus\mathbb H\). fate: Classical Clifford/quaternion algebra; the relation with normed division algebras is treated in \citet[Secs.~2.2--2.3]{baez2002octonions}. The dimension and quotient distinction follow directly from the monomial basis.

title: The scope of the cited self-dual cancellation results
notes: Hawking--Pope 1978 is cited for one-loop zero-mode contributions; Kallosh and Christensen--Duff for higher-order self-dual results. Four references are listed.

title: Complementary isotropic planes and the GL2 subgroup
notes: Prove the existence of transverse isotropic \(L,L'\), then prove that \(U(2,2)\) contains a copy of \(GL_2(\mathbb C)\).
statement: In a Hermitian space of signature \((2,2)\), choose positive orthonormal vectors \(p_i\) and negative orthonormal vectors \(q_i\). Their sums and suitable imaginary multiples of their differences give complementary isotropic two-planes with form matrix \(H=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&iI\\-iI&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Then \(g\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(g,(g^*)^{-1})\) is an injective homomorphism into \(U(H)\).
reconstruction: Direct block multiplication gives \(G^*HG=H\). The mixed pairings determine the conjugate inverse transformation of the second basis. Their reversed pairings are \(-i\), so the phrase all other scalar products zero means only the independent pairings.
fate: The exercise is solved by elementary Witt decomposition and the displayed block check; it belongs to preexisting indefinite-unitary linear algebra \citep[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Tube domains, real boundary and boundary strata
notes: \(S_\pm\) are positive/negative two-planes, with \((U-U^*)/i\) definite; \(M_0=\{U=U^*\}\) is their common skeleton.
statement: In a compatible graph convention, positivity of the restricted Hermitian form is equivalent to positive definiteness of \(\operatorname{Im}U=(U-U^*)/(2i)\); negativity is analogous. The real chart of maximal isotropic planes is \(\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)\), of real dimension four. The finite boundary of the positive tube has \(\operatorname{Im}U\ge0\) singular, including rank-one and rank-zero strata.
reconstruction: The Hermitian locus is the distinguished real boundary, not the entire topological boundary. Positive and negative planes are automatically transverse to the fixed isotropic complement; maximal isotropic planes need not be.
fate: Classical matrix-domain geometry underlying the Minkowski real form \citep[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}; the definiteness criterion follows by restricting \(H\) to a graph.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Transitivity and conformal compactification
notes: \(U(2,2)\) preserves \(S_+,S_-,M\) and acts transitively on each; \(M\) is the conformal compactification of Minkowski space.
statement: The group \(U(2,2)\) acts transitively on maximal positive, maximal negative and maximal isotropic complex two-planes. The last space is compact: in the positive/negative decomposition, each maximal isotropic plane is the graph of a unitary map, giving \(M\simeq U(2)\). Its dense Hermitian chart carries the Minkowski conformal class.
reconstruction: Transitivity follows by extending adapted bases to Hermitian isometries. \(U(2)\) is \((S^1\times SU(2))/\{\pm1\}\), so the compactification has the usual finite-cover convention; no unqualified \(S^1\times S^3\) identification is imposed.
fate: The compactification is preexisting twistor theory and is checked in \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Fractional-linear action on matrix coordinates
notes: For \(g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the action is \(U\mapsto(AU+B)(CU+D)^{-1}\).
statement: If a plane is represented by columns \(\binom{U}{I}\), block multiplication and renormalization give exactly \(g\cdot U=(AU+B)(CU+D)^{-1}\), on the open set where \(CU+D\) is invertible. Using columns \(\binom{I}{U}\) instead gives \((C+DU)(A+BU)^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The earlier graph-basis notation appears to use the opposite ordering. Both formulas express the same Grassmannian action after a consistent chart convention; the rational map is not defined on the whole affine chart for every \(g\).
fate: Elementary projective/Grassmannian linear algebra, directly checked by block multiplication; compare \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The affine chart stabilizer includes dilations
notes: The subgroup preserving \(G_0\), acting by \(U\mapsto aUa^*+b\), \(a\in GL_2(\mathbb C)\), \(b=b^*\), is said to be isomorphic to the Poincaré group.
statement: The displayed affine action preserves the Minkowski quadratic form up to the constant factor \(|\det a|^2\), because \(\det(a\,dU\,a^*)=|\det a|^2\det(dU)\). It is a similarity group including positive dilations. Restricting \(|\det a|=1\), and quotienting the scalar \(U(1)\) kernel, gives the connected Lorentz part together with translations.
reconstruction: For example \(a=2I\) sends \(U\) to \(4U\), which is not a Minkowski isometry. The covering relation between \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\) and the proper connected Lorentz group must also be distinguished from isomorphism.
fate: The classical conformal action is reviewed in \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}; the counterexample follows immediately from the notebook formula.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The determinant is the Minkowski quadratic form
notes: \(\det(dU)\) is the metric; the Pauli matrix uses coordinates \(u_0,u_1,u_3,u_4\), but the following line uses \(u_0,u_1,u_2,u_3\) and ends with a cube.
statement: For \(U=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}x_0-x_1&x_2+ix_3\\x_2-ix_3&x_0+x_1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(\det(dU)=dx_0^2-dx_1^2-dx_2^2-dx_3^2\). This is a quadratic form of signature \((1,3)\), whose polarization defines the Minkowski metric.
reconstruction: The relabelling of spatial coordinates must be made consistently. The final exponent \(3\), visible in the original PNG, is a faithful error and must be \(2\).
fate: This is an elementary determinant calculation in the standard spinor realization \citep[Sec.~3.1]{woit2021euclidean}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Intersecting twistor lines and the light cone
notes: All projective lines meeting a fixed line \(\ell_0\) satisfy \(\det(U^0-U)=0\); on the real slice this is the light cone.
statement: Two graph two-planes \(W_U,W_V\) meet nontrivially if and only if \(\ker(U-V)\ne0\), equivalently \(\det(U-V)=0\). For Hermitian \(U,V\), this means their Minkowski separation is null.
reconstruction: The statement concerns the graph chart; the Grassmannian incidence condition itself extends globally. The cone includes its vertex \(U=V\), where the intersection dimension jumps from one to two.
fate: Classical twistor incidence, also present in the earlier seminar occurrence 1978-455.1; checked in \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean} and directly by solving the graph intersection equations.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Correcting the point/ray correspondence
notes: One sentence claims a bijection between points of \(M\) and rays in \(N\); the following line correctly relates light rays on \(M\) to isotropic projective twistors.
statement: A point of compactified Minkowski space corresponds to a maximal isotropic two-plane in \(T\), hence to a projective line \(\mathbb P^1\) of null twistors. A projective null twistor corresponds to the null geodesic formed by all maximal isotropic two-planes containing that line in \(T\).
reconstruction: The first claimed bijection is dimensionally impossible: \(M\) has real dimension four, while the projective null-twistor space has dimension five. The incidence relation, with its different fibres, is the correct replacement.
fate: The standard correspondence is explicit in \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}. The contradiction is already visible between the two adjacent notebook sentences.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The status of curved twistor theory in 1979
notes: Twistor theory in curved space has yet to be worked out, although papers already exist.
statement: A general curved-spacetime extension is a broad programme, but a precise self-dual curved construction already existed before this lecture. It is therefore inaccurate to read the sentence as denying every curved twistor correspondence.
reconstruction: The nonlinear-graviton construction concerns constrained complex/self-dual geometry; it is not a solution for all real Lorentzian Einstein metrics.
fate: Penrose's \emph{Nonlinear gravitons and curved twistor theory} appeared in January 1976 \citep{penrose1976nonlinear}. Publisher metadata was opened; the full original theorem was not retrieved, so no detailed theorem formulation is assigned to that citation.

title: A higher-dimensional twistor analogue
notes: Contest: formulate a higher-dimensional generalization, with the hint line \(\rightsquigarrow\) flag.
statement: The instruction specifies neither the ambient dimension, real form, flag type, field equation nor the incidence property to preserve. One direct matrix generalization uses maximal isotropic \(m\)-planes in \(\mathbb C^{m,m}\), a Hermitian \(m\times m\) chart and \(U(m,m)\) fractional transformations.
reconstruction: That chart has real dimension \(m^2\), and \(\det(dU)\) has degree \(m\); it is a quadratic Lorentz form only when \(m=2\). Thus merely replacing two by \(m\) does not reproduce all four-dimensional features.
fate: The elementary extension explains one possible direction, but does not constitute a unique solution of the contest. No exact publication can be matched to the unspecified desired analogue.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains an open-ended programme in the notebook, not a uniquely determined open conjecture.

title: Parity in a graded vector space
notes: \(L=L_0\oplus L_1\); the notes call elements in either summand homogeneous and use parity \(\alpha(x)\in\mathbb Z_2\).
statement: For \(\mathbb K=\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), a super vector space is a direct sum \(L_{\bar0}\oplus L_{\bar1}\). A nonzero homogeneous vector in \(L_{\bar i}\) has parity \(i\); signs in tensor products are determined modulo two.
reconstruction: The zero vector belongs to both summands and has no uniquely determined parity. This harmless convention is made explicit.
fate: This is the preexisting language of superlinear algebra; compare \citet[Part I, pp.~90--130]{berezin1987superanalysis}. Publisher contents, rather than the full chapter, were checked.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The exterior algebra and its monomial basis
notes: \(\Lambda\) has generators \(1,\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), relations \(\xi_i\xi_j+\xi_j\xi_i=0\), ordered monomial basis, dimension \(2^N\), and \(fg=(-1)^{\alpha(f)\alpha(g)}gf\).
statement: Over a field of characteristic different from two, \(\Lambda=\bigwedge_{\mathbb K}\mathbb K^N\), with basis \(\xi_I=\xi_{i_1}\cdots\xi_{i_k}\) for ordered subsets \(I\), including \(\xi_\varnothing=1\). Its even and odd summands have dimensions \(2^{N-1}\) when \(N\ge1\); homogeneous elements supercommute.
reconstruction: The restriction on characteristic is supplied; it holds for the two fields named in the notes.
fate: Classical exterior algebra, already used throughout the earlier Berezin lectures and the 1978 BGG construction \citep[Sec.~2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The even Grassmann envelope
notes: The initial \(L\otimes\Lambda\) definition is cancelled. The replacement is \(L(\Lambda)=\{\sum a_ie_i:\alpha(a_i)=\alpha(e_i)\}=(\Lambda\otimes L)_{\bar0}\), a left \(\Lambda_0\)-module.
statement: For finite graded \(L\), \(L(\Lambda)=(\Lambda_{\bar0}\otimes L_{\bar0})\oplus(\Lambda_{\bar1}\otimes L_{\bar1})\). This is the even part of the graded tensor product, and is closed under multiplication by \(\Lambda_{\bar0}\).
reconstruction: The cancellation is substantive: the envelope is not the entire tensor product. Tensor multiplication for an algebra \(L\) requires the Koszul sign, or the equivalent coefficient-and-basis convention adopted in the lecture.
fate: The standard functor-of-Grassmann-points construction predates this talk; see \citet[Part I, linear algebra]{berezin1987superanalysis}, and the preceding seminar occurrences 1976-406.5--9.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Graph analogues of the even Grassmann algebra
notes: Gelfand proposes an analogue for every Dynkin diagram, with the ordinary example attached to \(A_n\); connected generators have product zero, disconnected ones a new product. He cites Functional Analysis 1979, no.~3.
statement: The recorded prescription is not a complete presentation: it omits whether generators commute, square to zero, obey further path relations, and what universal property the analogue must satisfy. It therefore does not determine a unique theorem or conjecture.
reconstruction: The exact cited paper can be identified as Gelfand--Ponomarev's model algebras, but identifying a citation does not identify the additional proposed Grassmann analogue.
fate: \citet[pp.~157--166]{gelfandponomarev1979model} is the exact volume/issue match, received 23 March 1979. Its graph-algebra setting supports the reference; no exact theorem equating the notebook prescription to its model algebras was verified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the all-Dynkin assertion remains underdetermined by these notes. It is not entered as an open problem.

title: Even block supermatrices
notes: \(L_{p,q}(\Lambda)\) has even entries in \(A_{11},A_{22}\), odd entries in \(A_{12},A_{21}\), and is an algebra.
statement: Fix a homogeneous basis of \(\mathbb K^{p|q}\). The even endomorphisms over \(\Lambda\) are the matrices \(A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}P&Q\\R&S\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) with \(P,S\) even and \(Q,R\) odd. With the lecture's left-module convention their composition is ordinary ordered matrix multiplication; parity is preserved.
reconstruction: An even supermatrix need not have all entries even. This distinction is essential: Problem 2 later asks about all-odd-entry matrices, not general odd endomorphisms of a \(p|q\) module.
fate: This is standard superlinear algebra; \citet[Part I, pp.~90--130]{berezin1987superanalysis} is a later systematic exposition, not evidence of a new 1979 theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Cyclicity of the supertrace
notes: \(\operatorname{str}A=\operatorname{tr}A_{11}-\operatorname{tr}A_{22}\) and \(\operatorname{str}(AB)=\operatorname{str}(BA)\).
statement: For even supermatrices \(A,B\) over a supercommutative algebra, \(\operatorname{str}(AB)=\operatorname{str}(BA)\). For homogeneous superendomorphisms of arbitrary parity the correct general relation is \(\operatorname{str}(AB)=(-1)^{|A||B|}\operatorname{str}(BA)\).
reconstruction: The even-envelope domain is retained; deleting it would make the unsigned cyclicity assertion false. Off-diagonal odd products change sign on interchange, cancelling the minus in the lower-block trace.
fate: Already part of the seminar's 1976-406.9 exposition and of Berezin's superlinear algebra \citep[Part I]{berezin1987superanalysis}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The Berezinian and its multiplicativity
notes: \(\operatorname{sdet}A=\det(P-QS^{-1}R)/\det S\) and \(\operatorname{sdet}(AB)=\operatorname{sdet}A\,\operatorname{sdet}B\).
statement: For an invertible even matrix over a finite Grassmann algebra, the bodies of \(P,S\) are invertible, hence so are \(P,S\). Define \(\operatorname{Ber}A=\det(P-QS^{-1}R)(\det S)^{-1}\in\Lambda_{\bar0}^{\times}\). It is multiplicative.
reconstruction: Invertibility, omitted at the definition, is necessary. This rational invariant differs from the ordinary determinant even when the matrix is block diagonal: it is \(\det P/\det S\).
fate: The Berezinian already occurs in \citet[formula~(3)]{berezinleites1975supermanifolds}; it recurs here after 1976-406.8--10. The primary metadata was rechecked and the displayed formula was checked algebraically against the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The 1|1 multiplicativity check
notes: For \(A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&\xi_1\\\xi_2&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the notes calculate \(\operatorname{Ber}A=1-\xi_1\xi_2\), \(A^2\), and \(\operatorname{Ber}(A^2)=1-2\xi_1\xi_2=(\operatorname{Ber}A)^2\).
statement: For odd generators \(\xi_1,\xi_2\) in characteristic zero, put \(t=\xi_1\xi_2\), so \(t^2=0\). Then \(A^2=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1+t&2\xi_1\\2\xi_2&1-t\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), and the Schur-complement formula gives \((1-3t)(1+t)=1-2t\).
reconstruction: This verifies the particular example. It does not by itself prove multiplicativity for every \(1|1\) matrix.
fate: A direct elementary instance of the preexisting Berezinian identity \citep[formula~(3)]{berezinleites1975supermanifolds}; the arithmetic is independently checked here.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The body map and invertibility
notes: The map \(m\) is evaluation at \(\xi=0\); the body of an even supermatrix is block diagonal.
statement: The augmentation \(m:\Lambda\to\mathbb K\) has nilpotent kernel \(J=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)\). An even supermatrix is invertible if and only if its body is invertible. Indeed, after factoring the body matrix, the remaining inverse is the finite Neumann series for \(1+K\), with \(K\in M_{p+q}(J)\).
reconstruction: The invertibility consequence is reconstructed to clarify the allowed change-of-basis group in the following theorem and problems.
fate: The body construction is standard in Berezin's superanalysis \citep[Part I, linear algebra]{berezin1987superanalysis}; the finite-series argument is given explicitly here.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Diagonalization when body eigenvalues are distinct
notes: Over \(\mathbb C\), if \(m(A)\) has distinct eigenvalues, then an invertible \(B\) makes \(BAB^{-1}\) diagonal.
statement: For a finite Grassmann algebra over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A\) be even and suppose all \(p+q\) eigenvalues of \(m(A)\), across both parity blocks, are distinct. There is an invertible even \(B\) with \(BAB^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_{p+q})\), where \(c_i\in\Lambda_{\bar0}\) has the corresponding eigenvalue as body.
reconstruction: Diagonalize the two body blocks first. At each positive Grassmann degree, remove the off-diagonal \((i,j)\) coefficient by division by the nonzero scalar \(\lambda_i-\lambda_j\); the nilpotent filtration terminates. This supplies a finite proof and specifies the parity of the conjugator.
fate: The statement belongs to standard supermatrix perturbation theory. The later Berezin book identifies the subject, but its full theorem was not retrieved; the proof here verifies the result independently \citep[Part I]{berezin1987superanalysis}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

statement: For fixed finite \(N,p,q\), classify even matrices \(A\in L_{p,q}(\Lambda_N)\) up to conjugation by invertible even matrices, without requiring distinct eigenvalues of the body. An effective canonical representative is one precise interpretation of an analogue of Jordan normal form.

title: Even commutants of all-odd-entry matrices
notes: Given \(A=(a_{ik})\) with every \(a_{ik}\in\Lambda_1\), describe all \(B=(b_{ik})\) with every \(b_{ik}\in\Lambda_0\) and \(AB=BA\). Four generators are related to Yang--Mills; independent entries are said to be tractable.
statement: For fixed \(n,N\), a specified \(A\in M_n(\Lambda_N^{\bar1})\), and a field of characteristic zero, determine the even subalgebra \(C_{\bar0}(A)=\{B\in M_n(\Lambda_N^{\bar0}):AB=BA\}\), including dimensions, bases and multiplication if desired.
reconstruction: Expand in the ordered monomial basis. This is the kernel of a finite \(\mathbb K\)-linear map \(B\mapsto AB-BA\), so the literal computation always has a terminating linear-algebra algorithm. A uniform structural description as \(A\) varies is a stronger question.
fate: The literal finite problem is solved by classical coefficient linear algebra: expand \(A,B\) in the ordered Grassmann monomials and take the kernel of \(B\mapsto AB-BA\). No specific later publication is needed for existence of this terminating procedure. Searches did not identify the precise historical structural description Berezin may have wanted. The chapter proves a complete bounded \(2\times2,\Lambda_4\) parametrization including cubic entries; no claim of historical novelty is made.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal finite computational task is resolved. A uniform structural normal form as \(A,n,N\) vary is a stronger interpretation, not an additional requirement specified in the manuscript, and is not labelled an open problem here.

title: Stable exterior modules and projective vector bundles
notes: Gindikin associates to a graded \(\Lambda(4)\)-module the differential \(a_1\xi_1+\cdots+a_4\xi_4\), whose cohomology is concentrated at zero, and says such modules modulo trivial ones classify instantons.
statement: For \(E=\mathbb C^4\), a finite graded \(\bigwedge E\)-module \(V\) gives a linear complex of bundles on \(\mathbb P(E)\) with differential \(\sum a_i\xi_i\). Modules whose fibre complexes have homology only in degree zero correspond to algebraic vector bundles, up to the stable equivalence generated by free exterior modules.
reconstruction: The anticommutation relations imply \(d^2=0\). A general module need not have the required fibre homology. Calling every resulting bundle an instanton drops the real structure and triviality on appropriate twistor lines required for the gauge-theoretic correspondence.
fate: \citet[Secs.~3--5, Theorems~1--3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles} already states the bundle correspondence, received 10 January 1978 and published in the 1978 volume. The recurrence is exact for bundles; the unqualified instanton identification is not. Compare 1977-437.6--12 and 1977-438.2--5.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Two distinct translation parametrizations
notes: A hypersurface germ \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb C^n\) is written both as \(\gamma_1+\cdots+\gamma_{n-1}\) and as \(\delta_1+\cdots+\delta_{n-1}\); permutations and translations are excluded.
statement: A translation parametrization of a smooth hypersurface germ is a local biholomorphism \((t_1,\ldots,t_{n-1})\mapsto\sum_i\gamma_i(t_i)\) onto the germ. Distinctness up to permutations and constant translations is a minimal condition; the classical converse needs stronger local nondegeneracy.
reconstruction: Without the immersion and local uniqueness conditions, arbitrary sums of curve germs can have smaller dimension or singularities.
fate: The classical subject and its precise genericity conditions are reviewed in \citet[Definitions~2.1--2.2]{little1983translation}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Theta divisors as sums of Abel curves
notes: For a smooth curve \(X\) of genus \(n\), the notes write \(\Theta=jX+\cdots+jX\), with \(n-1\) summands, and \(\Theta=K-\Theta\).
statement: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex curve of genus \(g\ge2\), \(j:X\to J(X)\) an Abel map based at \(p_0\), and \(W_{g-1}\) the image of effective divisors of degree \(g-1\). Then \(W_{g-1}\) is a translate of the theta divisor and is invariant under \(x\mapsto [K_X-(2g-2)p_0]-x\).
reconstruction: The symmetry follows from Riemann--Roch: an effective divisor \(D\) of degree \(g-1\) has \(h^0(K_X-D)=h^0(D)\). At regular points, two complementary effective divisors give the two local sums.
fate: This is preexisting Riemann theta-divisor theory; \citet[Example~4.1]{little1983translation} gives the exact translation-manifold example.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: When the two Abel curves are distinct
notes: \(X\ne-jX\) is said to be equivalent to nonhyperellipticity.
statement: For a smooth complex curve of genus \(g\ge2\), \(j(X)\) is a translate of \(-j(X)\) if and only if \(X\) is hyperelliptic. In the hyperelliptic case the two theta-divisor translation decompositions arising from inversion coincide.
reconstruction: The left-hand \(X\) is shorthand for its Abel image, and equality must be considered up to translation. For the converse, an inversion symmetry yields a fixed degree-two divisor class \(p+\iota(p)\), hence a degree-two map to \(\mathbb P^1\).
fate: Classical Abel-curve geometry; the hyperelliptic exception is explicit in \citet[Sec.~4, following Example~4.1]{little1983translation}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The Lie--Wirtinger converse with nondegeneracy
notes: All double translation surfaces are said to be theta divisors and their degenerations; the parenthesis claims that a small deformation is a theta-divisor germ.
statement: Take a smooth non-linear hypersurface germ in \(\mathbb C^n\) with two locally invertible sum parametrizations. Assume their \(2n-2\) tangent lines at the base point are distinct, every generating curve has acceleration transverse to the tangent hyperplane, and varying at least one first-system parameter while fixing the others changes every second-system parameter. Then the germ is a translate of the lift of an Abel-divisor locus in the generalized Jacobian of a reduced, connected canonical curve of degree \(2n-2\) and arithmetic genus \(n\).
reconstruction: The first two extra assumptions are Little's Definition~2.2; the last is condition (*) in Proposition~3.7. Singular or reducible curves give generalized Jacobians. Smoothability of every possible degeneration is not asserted here.
fate: Lie--Wirtinger is classical, not a new 1979 assertion. \citet[Corollary~3.5, Proposition~3.7, Theorem~3.9]{little1983translation} supplies a precise later proof and distinguishes the missing conditions. Its Theorem~5.1 recovers smooth nonhyperelliptic Jacobians when the ambient variety is principally polarized.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: A universal explanation of integrability by translation geometry
notes: Gelfand conjectures that all integrable systems have this theorem as their basis, and that it is the first of a large family of such theorems.
statement: No class of systems, notion of integrability, construction of an associated hypersurface, or meaning of being a basis is specified. There is no uniquely recoverable quantified conjecture.
reconstruction: The appearance of theta functions in algebraically integrable systems motivates the comment, but cannot turn a universal informal analogy into a theorem.
fate: The checked Lie--Wirtinger source concerns translation hypersurfaces, not all integrable systems \citep{little1983translation}. Its theorem therefore supplies no exact publication match for this universal programme.
present_status: As of November 2026, the recorded programme remains underdetermined; it is not labelled an open theorem.

title: The current group and its one-form Hilbert space
notes: \(G^X=C^\infty_0(X,G)\), with \(G\) compact simple; the one-form scalar product uses the Riemannian metric and the Killing form.
statement: For a smooth Riemannian manifold \(X\) and compact semisimple \(G\), let \(\mathcal G=C^\infty_c(X,G)\), meaning maps equal to the identity off a compact set. Complete \(\Omega^1_c(X,\mathfrak g)\) for \(\int_X \langle\omega_1,\omega_2\rangle_{g,B}\,d\mu\), with \(B\) an \(\operatorname{Ad}G\)-invariant positive inner product, for example minus the Killing form.
reconstruction: The Killing form itself is negative definite on a compact semisimple real Lie algebra. The sign is material to the Hilbert-space construction. The trace can be taken on either tangent or Lie-algebra endomorphisms because \(\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)\).
fate: This setting predates the lecture in \citet[Secs.~2--3]{albeveriohoeghkrohn1978energy}; the general geometric formulation is explicit in \citet[Sec.~6]{wallach1987gauge}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The infinite-dimensional Gaussian realization
notes: The notation is \(L^2(\mathcal H,\mu)\), with a Gaussian analogous to \(e^{-|x|^2/2}dx\), invariant under rotations and quasi-invariant under translations.
statement: On an infinite-dimensional separable real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), covariance \(I\) does not define a countably additive Gaussian Borel probability on \(\mathcal H\). Use an isonormal Gaussian process on a probability space, a nuclear dual containing \(\mathcal H\), or the symmetric Fock space over its complexification. Cameron--Martin translations are the vectors of \(\mathcal H\); abstract second quantization implements every orthogonal operator.
reconstruction: If independent coordinates had law \(N(0,1)\), their squared sum would diverge almost surely, so a sample would not lie in \(\ell^2\). An arbitrary orthogonal map need not act pointwise on a chosen Banach realization; its Gaussian unitary is nevertheless defined.
fate: \citet[Secs.~1 and~5]{wallach1987gauge} uses distribution spaces and Gaussian Hilbert spaces; \citet[Sec.~5]{albeverioetal2015brownian} gives the Fock/white-noise construction. The literal Hilbert-space probability notation is false.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The Maurer--Cartan cocycle and affine action
notes: \(\alpha(\varphi)\omega=\operatorname{Ad}\varphi\,\omega+\varphi^{-1}d\varphi\) is declared a group homomorphism.
statement: With \(\pi(\varphi)\omega=\operatorname{Ad}\varphi\,\omega\), the correct left cocycle is \(\beta(\varphi)=d\varphi\,\varphi^{-1}\), since \(\beta(\varphi\psi)=\beta(\varphi)+\pi(\varphi)\beta(\psi)\). Thus \(\alpha(\varphi)\omega=\pi(\varphi)\omega+\beta(\varphi)\) is a left affine action.
reconstruction: The displayed left Maurer--Cartan form instead obeys \((\varphi\psi)^{-1}d(\varphi\psi)=\operatorname{Ad}\psi^{-1}(\varphi^{-1}d\varphi)+\psi^{-1}d\psi\). It cannot be paired with \(\operatorname{Ad}\varphi\) in the stated left-action convention.
fate: The corrected cocycle appears in the energy construction \citep[Sec.~5]{wallach1987gauge}. Direct differentiation of a product independently verifies the correction; the original PNG confirms the manuscript order, so this is a faithful mathematical error.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The energy representation
notes: The notes form \(V_\varphi=U_{\alpha(\varphi)}\) from the Gaussian representation of the Euclidean group of \(\mathcal H\).
statement: For a real orthogonal representation \(\pi\) and continuous one-cocycle \(\beta\), the bosonic Fock representation satisfies \(V_g e(h)=\exp(-\|\beta(g)\|^2/2-\langle\pi(g)h,\beta(g)\rangle)e(\pi(g)h+\beta(g))\), with exponential vectors normalized by \(\langle e(h),e(k)\rangle=\exp\langle h,k\rangle\). Apply this to the current-group action and corrected Maurer--Cartan cocycle.
reconstruction: The cocycle identity proves the representation law and the exponential-vector inner product proves unitarity. Inner-product conventions may conjugate the displayed scalar in a complex realization; the real Gaussian model fixes it unambiguously.
fate: The energy representation was already constructed in \citet[Sec.~3]{albeveriohoeghkrohn1978energy}; its later Fock formulation is checked in \citet[Sec.~5]{albeverioetal2015brownian}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Irreducibility in dimension at least three
notes: Theorem~1: \(V\) is irreducible for \(\dim X\ge3\), attributed to Albeverio and Høegh-Krohn after earlier bounds five and four.
statement: For connected, orientable, paracompact smooth \(X\) of dimension at least three, compact semisimple \(G\), and the current-group energy representation from a Riemannian metric, smooth positive density and invariant positive Lie-algebra inner product, \(V\) is irreducible.
reconstruction: The lecture omits topological and measure hypotheses. Compactly supported currents and the full current group, rather than an arbitrary proper subgroup, are required.
fate: The soon-after joint paper \citet{albeveriohoeghkrohntestard1981irreducibility} includes Testard. Its result and earlier restrictions are documented and extended to this generality by the fully read \citet[Theorem~6.2]{wallach1987gauge}. The notebook is an October 1979 occurrence; a November 1979 conference presentation is not treated as the first circulation.

title: Reducibility in one dimension
notes: Theorem~2 states reducibility for \(\dim X=1\), followed by the Brownian path model.
statement: For the one-dimensional based path-group energy representation on a finite interval, the Brownian realization has non-scalar commuting right-action operators as well as the left-action representation. Hence the left representation is reducible for nontrivial \(G\).
reconstruction: Boundary and base-point conventions matter. This is the path model actually developed next in the notes, not an unqualified assertion for every subgroup or completion of a one-dimensional mapping group.
fate: The 1981 Albeverio--Høegh-Krohn--Testard paper records reducibility. A directly checked later proof uses commuting left/right Brownian representations and their energy equivalence \citep[Theorems~4.6 and~5.8]{albeverioetal2015brownian}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Irreducibility on a two-dimensional base
notes: \(\dim X=2\) is underlined and followed by a question mark.
statement: For a connected smooth Riemannian surface \(X\), compact semisimple \(G\), positive smooth measure density and positive invariant inner product on \(\mathfrak g\), decide irreducibility of the ordinary current-group energy representation for arbitrary such data.
reconstruction: The parameters are part of the question: a result after rescaling the covariance or coupling is not an all-parameter solution. Projective positive-energy representations of a semidirect product with time evolution are a different representation class.
fate: \citet[Theorem~6.2]{wallach1987gauge} proves irreducibility when \(d\mu=\rho\,d\operatorname{vol}\) and every root obeys \(\|\alpha\|_B>\sqrt{8\pi|\rho(x)|}\) at every \(x\). \citet{shimada2005irreducibility} claimed all dimensions, but \citet[p.~1]{hasebe2010white} identifies the invalid use of \(d\Phi=\beta(\exp\Phi)\) for nonabelian \(G\); \citet[Introduction]{ando2010local} also warns about the claim. The explicit \(SU(2)\) diagnostic in Section~\ref{dev:energy-diagnostic} illustrates the false differential identity; it is not a reducibility counterexample.
present_status: As of November 2026, the verified sources establish a genuine parameter-restricted theorem, while the unrestricted two-dimensional claim remains unresolved within the checked literature. Targeted recent searches found no verified repair; this is not an exhaustive assertion of current global openness.
worth: The remaining distinction is mathematically sharp: remove the root/covariance bound without importing a flawed nonabelian differential identity or changing the representation.

title: Stochastic development to Brownian paths on a group
notes: \(\eta^{-1}d\eta=db\); the notes say first to solve an ordinary equation and then transfer the measure. The displayed source space is accidentally \(C(\mathbb R^+,G)\).
statement: Let \(b\) be Brownian motion in \(\mathfrak g\) for a positive invariant metric, with \(b_0=0\). On a finite interval, the Stratonovich equation \(\eta^{-1}\circ d\eta=db\), \(\eta_0=e\), defines group Brownian motion and a measurable stochastic-development map from Wiener paths in \(\mathfrak g\) to continuous paths in \(G\).
reconstruction: Brownian paths are not differentiable; the equation needs a stochastic convention. The input is Lie-algebra path space, and the measure \(\mu_0\) belongs there. The group output measure is its pushforward.
fate: The construction is used in \citet[Sec.~4]{albeveriohoeghkrohn1978energy}; the modern formulation and stochastic logarithms are explicit in \citet[Sec.~2]{albeverioetal2015brownian}.

title: Quasi-invariance and the Brownian representation
notes: Left multiplication \(\eta\mapsto\varphi\eta\) is assigned a Radon--Nikodym derivative for \(\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^+,G)\), producing \(W_\varphi\).
statement: On based group Wiener space over \([0,T]\), multiplication by an absolutely continuous based path \(h\) with \(\int_0^T\|h^{-1}\dot h\|^2dt<\infty\) is quasi-invariant. Pullback multiplied by the square root of the appropriate Radon--Nikodym derivative is unitary.
reconstruction: The finite-energy condition is essential on an infinite interval. Smoothness alone on \(\mathbb R^+\) does not ensure finite energy. The initial value must preserve the based path space.
fate: The precise finite-energy path group and its density are given in \citet[Sec.~2]{albeverioetal2015brownian}; this is the qualified version of the construction already used in 1978.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: Equivalence of Brownian and energy representations
notes: Theorem: \(W_\varphi\cong V_\varphi\); the corresponding cocycle is the Maurer--Cartan form.
statement: For a compact connected Lie group and the based finite-energy path group on a finite interval, the Brownian representation is unitarily equivalent to the energy representation with the same invariant metric. Left and right Brownian versions are related by inversion.
reconstruction: The comparison is between matching path groups, interval conventions and covariance normalizations. Stochastic logarithm followed by Fourier--Wiener transform provides an explicit intertwiner.
fate: The equivalence is already central to \citet[Sec.~4]{albeveriohoeghkrohn1978energy}. The full later construction is \citet[Theorem~5.8]{albeverioetal2015brownian}; its 2015 preprint is corroboration, not the first announcement.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated, qualified result is established; the notebook wording is interpreted only with the hypotheses specified above.

title: The asserted type-III factor
notes: \([L_\infty\cup W_\varphi]''\) is called a factor of type~3.
statement: On \(L^2(Y,\mu)\) for a standard probability space, let \(L^\infty(Y,\mu)\) act by multiplication and let \(W\) be the quasi-regular unitaries of a nonsingular action. The commutant of \(\mathcal M=(L^\infty\cup W)''\) consists of invariant multiplication operators. If \(\mathcal M\) is a factor, that commutant is scalar, and \(\mathcal M=B(L^2(Y,\mu))\), a type-I factor.
reconstruction: Indeed the multiplication algebra is maximal abelian, so \(\mathcal M'\subset L^\infty\subset\mathcal M\). Factoriality forces \(\mathcal M'=\mathbb C I\). A group-measure-space crossed product acts on a different Hilbert space and must not be substituted silently.
fate: The literal assertion is disproved by this elementary commutant argument. Later type-III factorial path-group representations \citep{albeverioetal1983factorial} concern a different generated algebra; that work is an indirect thematic lead, not an exact repair.
present_status: As of November 2026, the printed operator-algebra expression is false under its stated realization. Which different factor construction was intended is not recoverable from the notebook.
